title: Curated identity alias
description: One row of data/curated/aliases.jsonl: a source string that denotes an entity, with the window the source is known to have used it. This is the table a reader consults to translate a source string — or a value in an older payload — into a canonical ID, and the table a rename pair shows up in as two rows with one entityId. `firstSeen`/`lastSeen` are observed use in the recorded corpus; where the corpus never dates a string, they are the window a declared alias in tools/dataset/rules/identity-aliases.json states. A row may share its `string` with another entity's row: `Wolf` names eight players, and which one answers depends on the date the source used it.

string.description: The source string, verbatim — the exact bytes the source used, including its casing and HTML entities (spec R7).

entityId.description: The canonical ID this string denotes.

entityName.description: The entity's current display name, repeated here so an alias row reads without a join (spec R12).

firstSeen.description: Earliest UTC date on which a recorded source row used this string for this entity. Null means the corpus does not date it, not that it was never used.

lastSeen.description: Latest UTC date on which a recorded source row used this string for this entity. Null means the corpus does not date it.

evidence.description: Why this mapping is believed: the source's own registry states it (`registry`), it is an old page in a Teams.RenamedTo chain (`rename`), it is a TeamRedirects/PlayerRedirects AllName (`redirect`), it is a player handle (`handle`), a recorded scoreboard row used it (`observed`), or rules/identity-aliases.json declares it (`declared`).
